triage.note: D10 defect 3, postmortem shape S2 again. The extracted item's text container rendered as a bare `<pre class="text">` (and, in Markdown mode, a bare `<div class="text md">`) — role `generic`, no name — so the pane holding the actual filing text was invisible to an accessibility-first reader. Red against the pre-D10 file (3cdfbf4), re-measured with the current check, four failures: `class="text md": role is None, want 'region'`; `class="text md": no accessible name naming the item — it carries neither aria-label nor aria-labelledby`; `class="text": role is None, want 'region'`; `class="text": no accessible name naming the item — it carries neither aria-label nor aria-labelledby`. Green once both carry role=region and an aria-label interpolating `${esc(it.item)}`. BOTH containers are pinned deliberately: they are the same slot in two view modes (ADR-032), so naming only the `<pre>` would let Markdown mode silently regress the fix. The label must INTERPOLATE the item code — a constant label would name all 23 items the same, which is the ambiguity shape this fix exists to remove, not a fix for it. PR #55 R2: the interpolation clause was satisfiable by a name that does not exist. `aria-labelledby="ghost-${esc(it.item)}"` interpolates the item code AND computes to an empty accessible name, because nothing in the file carries those ids — and it passed. `_named` now resolves every `aria-labelledby` token against an `id="…"` present in the same live file, so a dangling reference is no name. Red on that mutation, re-measured: `class="text md": no accessible name naming the item — aria-labelledby='ghost-${esc(it.item)}' resolves to no id present in this file, so the computed name is empty` and `class="text": no accessible name naming the item — aria-labelledby='ghost-${esc(it.item)}' resolves to no id present in this file, so the computed name is empty`. Two known gaps carried as debt rather than closed here: the resolution ceiling (PR #55 R11 — an id that EXISTS but names nothing is still accepted) and the missing `tabindex="0"` on these two scrollable regions (PR #55 R7). D14 (2026-08-28) closed the second gap: this case's input now carries `tabindex: "0"` per TD-145's acceptance, red-first alongside `ui-item-text-region-focusable`, whose note holds the observed pre-fix output.
